opening: This web shop lets anonymous internet users log in as any customer or administrator and read or change other customers' data. It is acceptable only as an isolated training target and must never hold real customer or payment data.

bullets.title: Login bypass and database takeover
bullets.body: SQL injection in login and product search lets unauthenticated visitors sign in as any user, including the administrator, and read database contents.

bullets.title: Customers can read and change others' records
bullets.body: Missing ownership checks (IDOR) let any signed-in customer view or modify other customers' orders, baskets and accounts.

bullets.title: New accounts can make themselves administrators
bullets.body: Registration accepts a role chosen by the caller (mass assignment), so anyone can create an account with administrator rights.

bullets.title: Forged logins for any account
bullets.body: The token signing key is committed to the source code, so anyone with repository access can mint valid logins for any user.

bullets.title: Server takeover through code execution
bullets.body: Profile handling runs attacker-supplied text as code on the server, exposing secrets, files and the database.

closing: Until these gaps are closed, the shop should run only in an isolated environment with disposable data and no exposure to real customers.
